title: Foreign Currency as a Trade and Bond Facility Criterion
summary: Foreign currency is increasingly utilized as a defining criterion for eligibility in specialized customs bond facilities. It serves as a benchmark for determining the nature of duty-paid/free bond institutions and as a condition for duty-free import privileges for specific industrial sectors.

evolution.eligibility: Expanded from a general medium of exchange to a specific prerequisite for industrial duty-free import incentives.
evolution.scope: Broadened to include industrial manufacturing sectors beyond retail bond shops.

timeline.change: Defined 'Duty Paid Bond' institutions based on their ability to sell goods to foreigners in exchange for foreign currency.
Linked duty-free import privileges for ship/dredger manufacturing industries to local supply orders payable in foreign currency.

Customs Act 2023: This law is formally defined as the Customs Act 2023.
Commissariat: A commissariat is an authorized establishment that sells food, cigarettes, liquor, and other beverages to foreign investors, workers, and technicians within export processing zones.
Duty Paid Bonded Warehouse: This refers to an establishment that sells bonded imported goods to foreign citizens residing or present in Bangladesh, subject to the payment of applicable duties and taxes in foreign currency.
Duty Free Bonded Warehouse: This refers to an establishment that sells bonded imported goods duty-free to arriving or departing passengers in exchange for foreign currency.
Diplomatic Bonded Warehouse: This refers to an establishment that sells bonded imported goods duty-free to diplomats or foreign citizens enjoying special privileges in exchange for foreign currency.
Schedule: This term refers to any schedule contained within these rules.
Deemed Export-Oriented Industrial Unit: This refers to an industrial unit that produces and supplies auxiliary materials to fully export-oriented industries through back-to-back letters of credit as a backward linkage industry.
Form: This term refers to any form prescribed within these rules.
Combined Deemed and Direct Export-Orient: This refers to an industrial unit that exports a portion of its products directly abroad and supplies the remaining portion as backward linkage to direct exporters via back-to-back letters of credit.
Warehouse License: This license is granted under Section 12 of the Customs Act 2023.
Licensee: This refers to any person, institution, or company that has been granted a license under these rules.
Licensing Authority: This refers to the licensing authority designated under Rule 3 of these rules.
Lien Bank: This refers to a bank approved by the licensing authority through which the licensee must conduct all import, export, and business operations.
Industrial Unit: This refers to an entity that processes raw materials, whether domestic or imported, to manufacture products for domestic consumption or for export.
Direct Export-Oriented Industrial Unit: This refers to an industrial unit that exports all of its produced or manufactured goods outside the geographical boundaries of the country in exchange for foreign currency.
General Bond: A general bond is an agreement executed by the licensee with the Government of Bangladesh for the purposes of Section 12(3) and Section 109 of the Act. It serves as a guarantee for the payment of prescribed amounts regarding the clearance, storage, and use of imported bonded goods.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue has issued an operational order regarding the procedures for importing raw materials under warehouse facilities.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: This order establishes the mandatory procedures for shipbuilding and dredger manufacturing industries that hold a warehouse license to import raw materials against local supply orders funded by international tenders and paid in foreign currency.

Customs Act 2023: Section 12 and the Second Schedule of this Act provide the legal authority for granting duty-free import privileges for raw materials under specific industrial conditions.
Duty-Free Import: Duty-free import of raw materials is permitted specifically for licensed shipbuilding or dredger manufacturing industrial units. This benefit applies to materials procured against local supply orders that are payable in foreign currency through international tenders.
